introduction.text: In this lesson, you will learn essential vocabulary and phrases for visiting the doctor in Spanish. You will also practice a simple dialogue that helps you describe symptoms and ask for help.
introduction.culturalNote: In many Spanish-speaking countries, it is common to greet the doctor with a handshake and a friendly smile, reflecting the importance of personal connection.

vocabulary.definition: A healthcare professional who diagnoses and treats illnesses.

exampleSentence.translation: The doctor helped me a lot.

vocabulary.tip: Remember that 'médico' is masculine; use 'la médica' for a female doctor.

vocabulary.definition: A meeting with a doctor to discuss health issues.
vocabulary.tip: Think of 'consulta' as a 'consultation' in English.

vocabulary.definition: A substance used to treat illnesses.

exampleSentence.translation: I need medicine for the cough.

vocabulary.tip: Remember that 'medicina' refers to the actual medicine, not the practice of medicine.
Think of 'síntoma' as a 'symptom' in English.

vocabulary.definition: An increase in body temperature, often indicating illness.

exampleSentence.translation: I have had a fever since yesterday.

vocabulary.definition: A written order for medication from a doctor.

exampleSentence.original: El médico me dio una receta.
exampleSentence.translation: The doctor gave me a prescription.

vocabulary.tip: Think of 'receta' as a 'recipe' for medicine.

grammar.title: Simple Future Tense
grammar.explanation: The simple future tense is used to express what will happen. In Spanish, you form it by adding endings to the infinitive verb. The endings are: -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án.

examples.translation: I will go to the doctor.
examples.breakdown: The verb 'ir' (to go) is in the simple future form 'iré' (I will go).

commonMistakes: Using the present tense instead of the future. Example: 'Voy al médico' (I am going) instead of 'Iré al médico' (I will go).
Forgetting to match the subject with the correct ending.

dialogue.title: At the Doctor's Office
dialogue.context: A patient visits the doctor to discuss their symptoms.

lines.translation: Hello, doctor. I am not well.
I have a fever and a cough.
Since when do you have a fever?

lines.text: Te voy a dar una receta.
lines.translation: I am going to give you a prescription.

culture.title: Healthcare in Latin America
culture.text: Healthcare systems vary widely across Latin America. Many countries have both public and private healthcare options, and it's common for people to have a personal relationship with their doctor.
culture.funFact: In Cuba, healthcare is free for all citizens, and the country has a high doctor-to-patient ratio.

keyPoints: Learned vocabulary related to visiting the doctor.
Engaged in a realistic dialogue about symptoms.
summary.nextSteps: Practice using the vocabulary in different sentences and review the simple future tense. You can also try to create your own dialogue based on a visit to the doctor.
